text:
Marcus Reed: heads up — perf-canary in staging flagged what looks like a kernel regression on `llama-3-70b-instruct` (A100-80GB) after the last runtime RC deploy.

Signal:
- slice: `staging/us-east`, `gpu_sku=a100-80gb`, `scheduler_mode=stable`, `streaming=false`
- p95 end-to-end latency: +14–18% (mostly in decode)
- tokens/sec: -11%

This is the first time I’ve seen it this clean (sample size ~1.2k runs, after warmup).

Link to Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-canary-model/perf-canary-model?var-model=llama-3-70b-instruct&var-region=us-east&var-env=staging

I pulled a quick profiler snippet below (from a canary pod) — looks like we’re hitting a different attention kernel than yesterday.

```text
run_id=canary-2025-01-11T22:05Z model=llama-3-70b-instruct gpu=a100-80gb runtime_build=rc-2025.01.11-3 git_sha=8f2c1b7
prefill_ms_p50=312 prefill_ms_p95=345 decode_ms_p50=41 decode_ms_p95=68
kernel_select.attn_kernel_id=fa2_sm80_v3
kernel_select.fallback_reason=

nsys summary (top kernels by time):
  38.6%  flash_attn_fwd_fa2_sm80_v3
  17.4%  rms_norm_fused
  12.1%  gemm_f16_tc

baseline (yesterday):
  kernel_select.attn_kernel_id=fa2_sm80_v2
  decode_ms_p95=58
```

Suspect PR range is whatever landed between rc-2025.01.10 and rc-2025.01.11. Anyone know what toggled v3 on for SM80?

perf-canary-bot: :rotating_light: *Perf Canary Regression (STAGING)*
Model: llama-3-70b-instruct
Slice: region=us-east gpu_sku=a100-80gb scheduler_mode=stable mode=non_streaming
Metric: p95_latency_ms
Current: 1420ms  Baseline(7d median): 1210ms  Delta: +17.3%
Window: 30m  Samples: 1268
Runtime: rc-2025.01.11-3 (git 8f2c1b7)
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/perf-canary-model/perf-canary-model?var-model=llama-3-70b-instruct&var-region=us-east&var-env=staging
Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Perf+Canary+Regression+Triage

Hiro Tanaka: thanks. `fa2_sm80_v3` shouldn’t be slower than v2 at those seq lengths… unless we’re missing the fused path and bouncing through an extra transpose.

Do we have the prompt shape for the canary run (prefill tokens / decode tokens)?

Marcus Reed: yep, from config:
- prefill: 1.5k tokens (± ~50)
- decode: 256 max, typical 180–220
- batch size target: 1 (canary pins it)

Omar El-Sayed: fwiw, `kernel_select.*` fields showing up are from https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/39141 (landed yesterday)

It’s possible v3 has been used before but we couldn’t see it.

Also can confirm canary requests are tagged `source=perf-canary`, so the logs you pasted are definitely canary path.

Noah Patel: +1 to Omar — we should validate whether this is *real* regression vs “visibility unlocked”.

Can someone check historical runtime logs (pre-39141) from staging? e.g. grep for kernel symbol names in nsys? Might be hard.

Hiro Tanaka: I’ll check in the kernel registry — I remember we enabled v3 behind a heuristic for certain head dims.

What’s the head_dim on llama3 70b? 128, right?

Marcus Reed: yep head_dim=128.

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler side should be stable; no changes in that RC besides the canary-safe priority thing earlier in the week.

If batch=1 pinned, shouldn’t be scheduler variance anyway.

Mateo Alvarez: can we confirm it reproduces on a single node consistently? i.e. not one noisy host.

Marcus Reed: I reran on 3 different staging nodes (forced by draining/recreating the canary pod). Same delta within a couple %. Looks persistent.

Omar El-Sayed: do we have deploy annotation for when `rc-2025.01.11-3` landed in staging?

deploy-bot: Deployed `runtime` to `staging/us-east`
- build: rc-2025.01.11-3
- git_sha: 8f2c1b7
- started: 2025-01-11 20:41 UTC
- finished: 2025-01-11 20:49 UTC
Diff: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/compare/1a0d9c4...8f2c1b7

Noah Patel: diff link is helpful. scanning quickly — there’s also https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/39166 (scheduler config pinning for canary) but that shouldn’t impact staging kernel choice.

Anything in that diff that touches attention kernel selection or thresholds?

Hiro Tanaka: looking at diff… there’s a commit that bumps the FA2 kernel pack version (submodule) + changes default “prefer_v3” threshold.

Might have been pulled in as part of the last kernel rollup.

Omar El-Sayed: if we have a canary nsys trace, can you paste the kernel launch params line for flash attention? Sometimes v3 uses a different tile size.

Marcus Reed: here’s the relevant excerpt (from nsys CLI export):

```text
flash_attn_fwd_fa2_sm80_v3<<<(120,1,1),(256,1,1),0,stream7>>>(...
  seqlen_q=214 seqlen_k=1536 head_dim=128 num_heads=64
  causal=1 dropout=0.0
)
```

And from the baseline trace I found from yesterday’s canary run (same prompt set):

```text
flash_attn_fwd_fa2_sm80_v2<<<(120,1,1),(256,1,1),0,stream7>>>(...
  seqlen_q=209 seqlen_k=1536 head_dim=128 num_heads=64
  causal=1 dropout=0.0
)
```

Hiro Tanaka: ok that’s apples-to-apples.

Hypothesis: v3 path is falling back internally for causal+head_dim=128 on SM80 when seqlen_k is “large-ish”, so it’s doing an extra pass. v2 might have the better causal optimization here.

We should try forcing v2 for that slice to validate.

Noah Patel: do we have a runtime flag to pin attention kernel? even just for staging canary.

Hiro Tanaka: there’s an env var for debug builds, but not exposed in prod configs. I can add a temporary override gated by `source=perf-canary` (similar to the kernel selection export gating).

But faster: I can locally reproduce on an A100 box and run microbench to compare v2 vs v3 for (k=1536, q~200).

Sofia Ivanova: if we’re gating by `source=perf-canary`, that’s acceptable overhead-wise, but we should keep it staging-only unless we decide to ship.

Mateo Alvarez: agreed. Let’s treat this as a real regression until proven otherwise. Next steps:
1) Hiro to confirm v3 perf issue on A100 for that shape.
2) If confirmed, disable v3 heuristic for sm80/head_dim=128 in the RC (or pin v2) and redeploy staging.
3) Marcus to re-run canary and confirm p95/tps return to baseline.

Marcus Reed: +1. I’ll also file a tracking ticket for the regression and link the grafana panel + traces.

Hiro Tanaka: can you drop the nsys file somewhere? even a `nsys stats` dump is fine.

Marcus Reed: yep, uploaded stats + the exported report here: https://drive.redwood.ai/engineering/serving-runtime/perf-canary/nsys/2025-01-11_llama3-70b_a100_sm80_v3_regression/

Omar El-Sayed: once Hiro has a fix/mitigation, can we annotate the canary dashboards with “kernel override active” so SRE doesn’t think we magically improved perf.

Noah Patel: also worth checking if this impacts other models on A100 (mixtral?) — canary should show if v3 gets picked elsewhere.

Marcus Reed: quick glance — mixtral 8x7b slice is flat; only llama3-70b is red right now.

Hiro Tanaka: ok. I’ll open a PR to revert the sm80 v3 heuristic for causal head_dim=128 (or narrow it). I’ll post link once up.

Mateo Alvarez: thanks all. keep this thread updated when we have a candidate PR + staging verify.

Marcus Reed: will do.
